doughnut: The baker rolled a warm, fried doughnut in sugar.
Would you like jam or cream inside your doughnut?
What a lovely ring-shaped doughnut with pink icing and sprinkles!
cough: When the dust tickled my throat, I began to cough.
Did you hear him cough loudly at the back of the library?
I had to cough to clear a crumb from my throat.
tough: This old rope is strong and tough, so it will not snap.
Is the shell of a coconut really hard and tough?
The gardener wore tough gloves to cut the prickly bushes.
roughly: The jar holds roughly a hundred marbles, but I did not count them.
Roughly how many biscuits are in that big tin?
The walk to school takes roughly ten minutes.
bought: She counted her coins at the till and bought two apples.
Dad sold his old bike, and I bought it from him.
I saved my pocket money for weeks and bought a football at last!
thoughtful: A thoughtful neighbour watered our plants while we were on holiday.
My thoughtful friend saved me a seat on the bus.
Sharing your umbrella with a classmate was very thoughtful.
brought: I brought my football to the park so we could all play.
Everyone brought a book from home for the class swap.
My gran came by train and brought her knitting with her.
plough: The tractor pulled the plough, turning the soil into neat rows.
In the old picture, a horse was pulling a plough.
Behind the barn stood a rusty plough covered in weeds.
drought: No rain fell for weeks, and the long drought dried the garden.
During the drought, the grass turned brown and the pond shrank.
Is there a hosepipe ban because of the drought?
throughout: Throughout the lesson, the class sat quietly and listened.
I wore my red scarf throughout the cold winter.
Our dog stayed calm throughout the long film.

rejected.s: My grandad likes to cough politely before he starts to speak.

rejected.s: Please turn your head and cough into your elbow.
rejected.reason: checker: Coughing into your elbow is a germ-hygiene message that suggests illness, so it is dropped as doubtful.

rejected.s: My gran bought tickets for the puppet show last week.
rejected.reason: checker: Gran brought tickets makes equal sense, so the gap is not unique. (also fits: brought)

rejected.s: We paid at the till, and then we bought new trainers.
rejected.reason: checker: Paying first and then buying is the wrong order and reads unnaturally.

rejected.s: He bought a birthday card, and the shopkeeper wrapped it up.
rejected.reason: checker: Brought a card to the shopkeeper could also fit, so the gap is not clear enough. (also fits: brought)

rejected.s: What does a plough do to the soil in a field?
rejected.reason: machine rule 5: word overlap with the meaning is 100%

rejected.s: The shop sold the last loaf, so we bought it.
rejected.reason: checker: The logic is muddled (if the shop sold the last loaf, who bought it?), and 'brought it' (home) could also fit. (also fits: brought)

rejected.s: Which kite would you have bought if the price was lower?
rejected.reason: checker: The conditional is ungrammatical; it should be 'had been lower'.
